meta.scope: Read-only static full-stack audit of backend, frontend, database schema, desktop app, deployment configuration and HRMS business rules.
notTested: Live production behaviour and authentication against real accounts
Windows NSIS installer and macOS DMG execution, installation and update
Live database migration history and schema drift
Packaged renderer CORS Origin header and file:// CSP interception
meta.secretsPolicy: No secret values are reproduced in this inventory. Only file and line references are given.

findings.title: Public repository tracks production database dumps with PII, payroll and credential material
findings.evidence: git ls-files lists three tracked SQL dumps (212,327 / 470,988 / 235,116 bytes). Dumps contain INSERT statements for Employee, Payslip, SalaryStructure, TaxDeclaration, EmployeePaymentInfo, RefreshToken and User including passwordHash and mfaSecret. GitHub API reports private=false, visibility=public.
findings.impact: Irreversible disclosure of employee identity documents, bank details, salary/tax data, password hashes, MFA secrets and session token hashes to anyone on the internet.
findings.rootCause: Database dumps produced inside the repository and committed; .gitignore does not exclude *.sql, db-backups/ or mariadb/; no secret scanning.
findings.remediation: Make repository private immediately; purge dumps from working tree and all history (git filter-repo); rotate every credential present; revoke all refresh tokens; add gitleaks/trufflehog pre-commit blocking; notify affected employees.

findings.title: Published default passwords and plaintext credential scripts
findings.evidence: HOSTINGER.md contains a Default Credentials table for super-admin, HR manager and an employee. Four backend scripts hardcode the same plaintext passwords; seed_remote.js creates admin@acme.com with isSuperAdmin true. Values redacted in this inventory.
findings.impact: If any password was not rotated, the public repository hands an attacker super-admin/HR access. admin@acme.com is privileged both in the seed script and in group-access.util.ts.
findings.rootCause: Bootstrap scripts committed with literal secrets and human-written deployment documentation containing real values.
findings.remediation: Rotate all three accounts and disable admin@acme.com; delete the scripts and credential table from history; replace with env-driven bootstrap that refuses production; force password change on first login.

findings.title: Group-wide privilege granted by role-name substring, system flag and hardcoded emails
findings.evidence: isGroupWideUser returns true for isSuperAdmin, three hardcoded emails, any role with isSystem true, and any role whose lowercase name contains admin, group or hr admin. CompanyScopeGuard:24 short-circuits all tenant checks for these users.
findings.impact: Any tenant-level HR Admin role name grants cross-tenant read and often write access to employees, salaries, attendance, leave and documents. Multi-tenant isolation defeated.
findings.rootCause: Authorization derived from mutable display strings and an overloaded isSystem flag instead of an explicit capability.
findings.remediation: Introduce explicit User.isGroupAdmin or organization:manage_all permission; remove email allow-list; make role.isSystem mean non-editable only; add negative integration tests across tenants.

findings.title: GET /companies/:id/employees enumerates any tenant
findings.evidence: Handler has no @Permissions decorator; PermissionsGuard returns true when no metadata exists (permissions.guard.ts:55). Service where clause is identical in both groupWide branches: { companyId } from the path, never the caller's company.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can enumerate any company's employees by id.
findings.rootCause: Default-allow permission guard plus missing tenant check in the service.
findings.remediation: Require organization:view permission; verify companyId is in the caller's allowed set unless genuine group admin; return 404 to avoid tenant enumeration.

findings.title: GET /group/employees returns every employee in every tenant
findings.evidence: Handler has no @Permissions decorator. Service computes groupWide then queries employee.findMany({ where: { isSystem: false } }) with no company filter.
findings.impact: Full cross-tenant employee directory including company and department to any authenticated user.
findings.rootCause: No permission metadata, no company filter, unused groupWide value.
findings.remediation: Gate behind explicit group-admin capability; remove from tenant controller or return 403 for non-group users; require company filter otherwise.

findings.title: GET /documents/all returns every document record in every tenant
findings.evidence: listAll() has no @Permissions decorator and no company scope. CompanyScopeGuard cannot help because the request carries no employeeId or record id. Service is employeeDocument.findMany({ orderBy }) with no where clause.
findings.impact: Every document row in every tenant (employee id, type, fileUrl, signature state) readable by any authenticated user; direct document disclosure where fileUrl is public.
findings.rootCause: Missing PermissionsGuard and missing tenant filter on a bulk list endpoint.
findings.remediation: Add PermissionsGuard + documents:view; scope by employee.companyId; use signed short-lived download URLs.

findings.title: Leave apply/balance/monthly-balance fall back to unscoped employee lookups
findings.evidence: After a company-scoped findFirst, the code falls back to employee.findUnique({ where: { id: employeeId } }) for every caller, not only group-wide users. leave.controller.ts uses JwtAuthGuard + PermissionsGuard but not CompanyScopeGuard.
findings.impact: A user in tenant A can read or adjust tenant B leave balances and create leave requests against foreign employees.
findings.rootCause: Group-wide fallback applied unconditionally; controller missing tenant guard.
findings.remediation: Remove the fallback; throw NotFound when groupWide is false and the employee is outside companyId; add CompanyScopeGuard; add cross-tenant tests.

findings.title: Project/task writes have no tenant or permission check
findings.evidence: Controller uses only JwtAuthGuard. POST /projects/:id/tasks and POST /projects/tasks/:taskId/status pass path ids directly to Prisma with no company or permission check.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can add tasks to, or change the status of, any tenant's project tasks.
findings.rootCause: Missing CompanyScopeGuard and missing ownership check in service.
findings.remediation: Add CompanyScopeGuard; verify project ownership; require projects:edit; validate status against an enum.

findings.title: Announcements list queries all companies regardless of tenant
findings.evidence: list() computes groupWide then loads every company id and queries companyId: { in: allCompanyIds }. listAll() does the same without the isActive filter. groupWide is unused.
findings.impact: Every employee reads every tenant's announcements; group-wide create clones content into all tenants.
findings.rootCause: Tenant filter replaced by an all-company query; computed authorization value ignored.
findings.remediation: Use groupWide ? {} : { companyId }; require explicit broadcast permission for group-wide create.

findings.title: assign-employees moves arbitrary employee ids across tenants
findings.evidence: Endpoint requires organization:edit but the service accepts arbitrary employeeIds and writes companyId = target without verifying current ownership or writing history/audit.
findings.impact: A tenant admin with organization:edit can move another tenant's employees into their own tenant or out of it.
findings.rootCause: Bulk mutation without per-record ownership validation.
findings.remediation: Load each employee, assert current companyId is permitted, write EmployeeCompanyHistory in a transaction, emit audit log.

findings.title: PermissionsGuard defaults to allow when no decorator is present
findings.evidence: if (!required || required.length === 0) return true; converts a forgotten decorator into any-authenticated-user access.
findings.impact: Root cause of SEC-004/005/006 and other undecorated routes; systemic authorization failure.
findings.rootCause: Fail-open default in the permission guard.
findings.remediation: Default-deny; add @Public() for unauthenticated routes and explicit @SelfService/@AnyAuthenticated markers; fail startup if a non-public handler has no metadata.

findings.title: Device enforcement uses entirely client-supplied context
findings.evidence: buildContext prefers the request body device object, then a decoded X-Device-Context header, then individual headers. platform, arch, osVersion, isVirtualMachine and signals are all attacker-controlled.
findings.impact: The server-side Windows 10/11 x64 control is bypassable by any scripted client; only the desktop gate remains, and it fails open (DESK-002).
findings.rootCause: Trusting client telemetry as an enforcement input without attestation.
findings.remediation: Treat device context as advisory; if enforcement is required use signed device attestation bound to a TPM/keystore key.

findings.title: Access and refresh tokens stored in localStorage
findings.evidence: Both tokens are written to localStorage and read back for every request.
findings.impact: Any XSS or malicious dependency can exfiltrate a 7-day refresh token in an app handling payroll and statutory PII.
findings.remediation: Keep access token in memory; store refresh token in OS secure storage on desktop and httpOnly cookie on web; add strict CSP.

findings.title: No logout/revocation endpoint; 7-day refresh tokens remain valid
findings.evidence: Controller exposes register, login, refresh, mfa/enable and me only. Client logout only removes localStorage. JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN is 7d.
findings.impact: A stolen refresh token remains usable after the user logs out; no user-initiated session termination.
findings.rootCause: Missing logout/logout-all endpoints and no client-side revocation call.
findings.remediation: Add POST /auth/logout and /auth/logout-all that revoke the presented refresh token/session; shorten refresh lifetime; expose active sessions UI.

findings.title: Generated employee password is the lowercased employee code
findings.evidence: const generatedPassword = !password ? dto.employeeCode.toLowerCase() : undefined;
findings.impact: Sequential employee codes produce guessable initial passwords with no forced change.
findings.remediation: Generate a cryptographically random temporary password, deliver out-of-band, force change at first login.

findings.title: Hardcoded privileged email addresses in authorization code
findings.evidence: Three literal email addresses return true from isGroupWideUser, including admin@acme.com which seed_remote.js creates.
findings.impact: Permanent bypass that survives role changes and cannot be revoked through the UI.
findings.rootCause: Emergency/backdoor bypass left in production code.
findings.remediation: Remove the allow-list; use explicit capabilities.

findings.title: CORS falls back to trusting every *.vercel.app and *.onrender.com origin
findings.evidence: When CORS_ORIGINS is unset, the allow function accepts any origin matching the vercel.app and onrender.com suffixes.
findings.impact: Any attacker-controlled deployment on those shared domains is trusted by the API.
findings.rootCause: Convenience wildcard fallback in production-capable code.
findings.remediation: Require CORS_ORIGINS in production and fail boot when unset; remove suffix matching.

findings.title: MFA can only be enabled; no verify, disable or recovery flow
findings.evidence: Only an mfa/enable route exists. No TOTP verification on login, no disable, no recovery codes.
findings.impact: Users can enter an MFA state they cannot complete or recover from; security value is illusory.
findings.remediation: Implement TOTP verify at login, recovery codes, disable with re-authentication, and audit events.

findings.title: Document upload accepts a client-supplied fileUrl with no type or size validation
findings.evidence: upload(employeeId, type, fileUrl) persists the caller-provided URL directly; no MIME, size, origin or malware check.
findings.impact: Arbitrary external or malicious content can be attached to employee records and later served to HR users.
findings.remediation: Server-side upload with MIME/size limits, signed storage URLs and malware scanning.

findings.title: Any same-tenant user can e-sign a document as another employee
findings.evidence: eSignDocument takes employeeId from the request body and records the signature without binding it to the authenticated user's own employee record.
findings.impact: Forged e-signatures on HR documents; audit trail attributes signature to the victim.
findings.rootCause: Signer identity taken from client input.
findings.remediation: Bind signer to user.employeeId; require consent capture; reject mismatched employeeId; audit signer, IP and hash.

findings.title: Bulk PII reads write no audit record
findings.evidence: AuditLog writes were found only on mutation paths; list endpoints examined do not emit an audit event.
findings.impact: A bulk exfiltration of employee or document data cannot be reconstructed from logs.
findings.rootCause: Audit logging scoped to writes only.
findings.remediation: Log actor, route, filters and result count for sensitive bulk reads; add an admin audit viewer.

findings.title: decrypt() returns ciphertext silently on GCM authentication failure
findings.evidence: The catch block returns the input value rather than throwing or recording a failure.
findings.impact: Tampered or wrongly-keyed data is passed to payroll and UI layers as if decrypted, hiding key rotation errors.
findings.rootCause: Fail-open error handling in a crypto boundary.
findings.remediation: Throw or return a typed error; emit a metric/alert; add a migration check for undecryptable rows.

findings.title: No secret-scanning or pre-commit guard for dumps, .env and credential scripts
findings.evidence: No gitleaks/trufflehog step in CI and no pre-commit hook; .gitignore does not exclude SQL dumps.
findings.impact: The SEC-001/SEC-002 class of leak can recur.
findings.remediation: Add secret scanning to CI and pre-commit; block *.sql, *.dump, db-backups/, .env* except .env.example.

findings.title: Tenant scoping is per-endpoint; only 17 of 36 controllers use CompanyScopeGuard
findings.evidence: 26 of 36 controllers use PermissionsGuard, 35 of 36 use JwtAuthGuard, but only 17 use CompanyScopeGuard. Remaining controllers rely on each service remembering to filter.
findings.impact: New endpoints are exposed by default; the P0/P1 cross-tenant findings are instances of this pattern.
findings.remediation: Apply CompanyScopeGuard globally with an opt-out, or inject companyId via Prisma middleware; add an architecture test that fails when a tenant-scoped route lacks both guards.

findings.title: No health or readiness endpoint
findings.evidence: No /health or /ready route; no Terminus module.
findings.impact: Render and external monitoring cannot distinguish a live process from one with a broken database connection.
findings.remediation: Add /health (liveness) and /ready (DB + migration check).

findings.title: No OpenAPI/Swagger documentation for 367 endpoints
findings.evidence: No @nestjs/swagger dependency or SwaggerModule setup.
findings.impact: Client/server drift such as API-007 is undetectable without reading both codebases.
findings.remediation: Add @nestjs/swagger, annotate DTOs, publish the spec and generate the frontend client from it.

findings.title: Inline object and any-typed bodies bypass class-validator
findings.evidence: Handlers type bodies as inline object literals or any, so ValidationPipe's whitelist never runs.
findings.impact: Mass assignment and type confusion; invalid data reaches services.
findings.rootCause: No DTO classes for many mutations.
findings.remediation: Define DTO classes with class-validator for every mutation; forbid inline body types in review.

findings.title: @Body('primitive') endpoints bypass validation entirely
findings.evidence: Reading a single primitive from the body bypasses both DTO validation and whitelist stripping.
findings.impact: Unvalidated values such as task status strings reach the database.
findings.rootCause: Primitive body extraction used for convenience.
findings.remediation: Use DTOs for all mutations; validate enums explicitly.

findings.title: Global throttle 100/min; no per-account lockout
findings.evidence: Auth endpoints have a 5/min IP throttle but no account-level backoff or CAPTCHA.
findings.impact: Distributed credential stuffing across IPs is not mitigated.
findings.remediation: Add per-account exponential backoff, CAPTCHA after N failures and alerting.

findings.title: Client calls GET /leave/monthly-allocation but backend handler is @Post
findings.evidence: Client helper issues a GET with no method option; the controller declares @Post('monthly-allocation').
findings.impact: The admin 'run monthly allocation' action always fails.
findings.rootCause: No contract test between client and server.
findings.remediation: Send method POST; add a contract test asserting method and path.

findings.title: Several list endpoints have no pagination or hard cap
findings.evidence: findMany calls without take/skip on tenant-wide collections.
findings.impact: Memory and latency blow up as data grows; bulk PII exposure.
findings.remediation: Enforce hard caps and cursor pagination on all list endpoints.

findings.title: settings/config accepts untyped unknown values
findings.evidence: Body typed as Record<string, unknown> and persisted without schema validation.
findings.impact: Corrupt or malicious settings can break features silently.
findings.remediation: Define a schema per config key and validate on write.

findings.title: Duplicate alias routes increase surface (salary-structure vs structure)
findings.evidence: Two route decorators map to the same handler behaviour.
findings.impact: Larger attack surface and client confusion; one alias can be missed in reviews.
findings.remediation: Deprecate one alias with a sunset date.

findings.title: No idempotency key for payroll run or monthly allocation
findings.evidence: No Idempotency-Key handling and no unique constraint preventing duplicate cycles/slips.
findings.impact: Retries or double clicks can create duplicate payouts or allocations.
findings.remediation: Add idempotency keys plus DB uniqueness (see DB-003).

findings.title: Error response shape is inconsistent
findings.evidence: Some paths throw ForbiddenException with a string, others with an object, others return Nest defaults.
findings.impact: Clients cannot reliably distinguish causes or show correct messages.
findings.remediation: Add a global exception filter with stable error codes and a documented shape.

findings.title: No deprecation or versioning policy beyond the v1 prefix
findings.evidence: URI version v1 is set globally; no policy for breaking changes or deprecation headers.
findings.impact: Clients break without warning.
findings.remediation: Document versioning and emit Deprecation/Sunset headers.

findings.title: No enableShutdownHooks; Prisma disconnect not wired to process signals
findings.evidence: Nest app does not call enableShutdownHooks and PrismaService does not implement OnModuleDestroy.
findings.impact: In-flight requests and DB connections are cut abruptly on deploy/restart.
findings.remediation: Call app.enableShutdownHooks(); implement OnModuleDestroy with $disconnect.

findings.title: Login page calls logout() on every mount
findings.evidence: useEffect(() => { useAuthStore.getState().logout(); }, []);
findings.impact: Revisiting /login destroys a valid session even when the refresh token is still valid.
findings.rootCause: Defensive logout placed in a render-lifecycle hook.
findings.remediation: Remove the effect; clear state only on explicit logout.

findings.title: activeCompanyId read from stale storage; switchCompany has no call sites
findings.evidence: Every request reads activeCompanyId from localStorage; a repository-wide search finds zero call sites for switchCompany or CompanySelector.
findings.impact: Multi-company users see the wrong tenant; after a user switch on a shared machine requests can target the previous tenant.
findings.rootCause: Company context never populated or switched after login.
findings.remediation: Populate activeCompanyId from login/me; call switchCompany from the selector; clear on logout; read from store not raw storage.

findings.title: Leave screens use relative /api/v1 fetch and wrong response shape
findings.evidence: Direct fetch('/api/v1/employees?...') bypasses API_BASE and then reads json.data.items, which is not the client response shape.
findings.impact: Employee dropdowns are empty in both the packaged app (file:///C:/api/v1/...) and on Vercel (SPA rewrite returns index.html).
findings.rootCause: Ad-hoc fetch instead of the shared API client.
findings.remediation: Use employeesApi/api(); correct the response shape; add a component test.

findings.title: Monthly allocation client uses GET against a POST endpoint
findings.evidence: leaveApi.monthlyAllocation builds a query string and calls api() with no method option.
findings.impact: The run-allocation action always fails.
findings.remediation: Pass { method: 'POST' }; add a contract test.

findings.title: Employee login-management UI is shown to non-super-admins
findings.evidence: Create-login, reset-password and toggle-login controls render without an isSuperAdmin check, while the backend guards them with SuperAdminGuard.
findings.impact: Non-super-admins get 403s and a confusing UX.
findings.rootCause: UI capability checks not aligned with backend guards.
findings.remediation: Gate controls on the same capability the backend enforces.

findings.title: Navigation permissions use role-name substrings, contradicting backend grants
findings.evidence: Menu visibility is derived from role-name substring checks rather than the permission list returned by the server.
findings.impact: Users see menus they cannot use or miss menus they are entitled to.
findings.rootCause: Duplicated authorization logic in the client.
findings.remediation: Drive navigation from the server-provided permission list.

findings.title: role.isSystem treated as super-admin in the frontend
findings.evidence: The route guard treats role.isSystem as equivalent to super-admin, which the backend does not do.
findings.impact: System roles see admin UI they cannot actually use; inconsistent authorization model.
findings.remediation: Use explicit permissions from the server; make isSystem mean non-editable only.

findings.title: Zero frontend automated tests; no test runner configured
findings.evidence: Scripts contain only dev, build, preview and lint; no test script or test dependency.
findings.impact: Regressions such as FE-001, FE-003 and FE-004 ship undetected.
findings.remediation: Add Vitest + Testing Library for units and Playwright for E2E; wire into CI.

findings.title: 1,663 any / as any occurrences weaken type safety
findings.evidence: Repository-wide grep counts 1,663 occurrences.
findings.impact: Type system cannot catch API shape bugs such as FE-003.
findings.rootCause: any used to bypass API typing.
findings.remediation: Enable strict incremental typing; generate types from the API schema.

findings.title: Monolithic route components (1,726 / 1,462 / 1,216 / 779 lines)
findings.evidence: Four components exceed 700 lines, with OrganizationPage at 1,726.
findings.impact: Hard to review and test; re-render hotspots; blocks route-level code splitting.
findings.remediation: Split by feature, extract hooks, lazy-load routes.

findings.title: refetchOnMount always plus window-focus refetch causes repeated list reloads
findings.evidence: QueryClient defaults set refetchOnMount: 'always' and refetchOnWindowFocus: true with no meaningful staleTime.
findings.impact: Every tab switch reloads lists, increasing API load and UI flicker.
findings.remediation: Set staleTime, disable refetchOnMount always, invalidate targeted queries after mutations.

findings.title: Multiple catch blocks swallow errors without user feedback
findings.evidence: Several catch blocks set an empty list or do nothing; no toast or error state.
findings.impact: Users see empty screens with no explanation; failures are invisible to support.
findings.rootCause: Defensive catch with no error surface.
findings.remediation: Surface error states, log to telemetry, add a shared error handler.

findings.title: Vercel deployment has no CSP, HSTS, frame or referrer headers
findings.evidence: Config contains only SPA rewrites; no headers block.
findings.impact: The web deployment is not hardened against clickjacking, referrer leakage or script injection.
findings.rootCause: Headers not configured at the edge.
findings.remediation: Add CSP, HSTS, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.

findings.title: No per-route error boundary; only one global boundary
findings.evidence: A single ErrorBoundary wraps the whole app.
findings.impact: One component crash blanks the entire application.
findings.remediation: Wrap route subtrees with boundaries and offer retry.

findings.title: 13 production console.* calls
findings.evidence: Grep finds 13 console statements in shipped source.
findings.impact: Noisy console and possible information leakage in production builds.
findings.remediation: Route through a logger and strip in production.

findings.title: Icon-only controls and modals lack focus management and ARIA labels
findings.evidence: Static review finds icon buttons without aria-label and modals without focus traps; no accessibility audit executed.
findings.impact: Screen-reader and keyboard users cannot reliably operate the app.
findings.rootCause: Accessibility not part of the component contract.
findings.remediation: Add labels, focus traps, escape handling; run axe in CI.

findings.title: CompanySelector component is dead code
findings.evidence: No imports or call sites anywhere in the repository.
findings.impact: Confusion for maintainers; company switching appears implemented but is not.
findings.remediation: Delete or wire it into the layout.

findings.title: Overnight shift end time is built on the same calendar day
findings.evidence: shiftStart and shiftEnd both use wall.y, wall.m, wall.d; for 22:00-06:00 shiftEnd precedes shiftStart.
findings.impact: Negative required minutes; overtime, late and early-exit calculations are wrong for night shifts.
findings.rootCause: No day rollover when end time is less than start time.
findings.remediation: Add one day to shiftEnd when end <= start; add tests for 22:00-06:00 and 00:00-08:00.

findings.title: Attendance date keys use server-local time, not company timezone
findings.evidence: The attendance day is computed with new Date() and new Date(y, m, d) in the server timezone even though the company timezone is used elsewhere.
findings.impact: A 23:30 IST punch on a UTC server can land on the previous day and split shifts across rows.
findings.remediation: Derive startOfDay from the company timezone; store UTC plus a canonical dateKey.

findings.title: Payroll applies the latest salary structure even if effective in the future
findings.evidence: salaryStructures relation uses orderBy effectiveFrom desc take 1 with no effectiveFrom <= periodEnd filter.
findings.impact: A revision effective next month changes this month's pay.
findings.remediation: Filter effectiveFrom <= monthEnd; add a regression test with a future-dated revision.

findings.title: Old-regime tax inputs omit rent, metro type, 80C, 80D and home-loan interest
findings.evidence: TaxInput is built from basic/hra/da/conveyance/medical/specialAllowance plus regime only; declaration values are never loaded.
findings.impact: Old-regime employees are systematically over-taxed and declared investments have no effect.
findings.rootCause: TaxDeclaration data not joined into the payroll calculation.
findings.remediation: Load declarations for the financial year, map to TaxInput, add golden tests.

findings.title: Section 87A rebate implemented as a cliff without marginal relief
findings.evidence: if (taxableIncome <= 1200000) baseTax = 0; above the threshold the full slab tax applies.
findings.impact: One rupee above the threshold can cost roughly 62,400 in tax.
findings.rootCause: Rebate modelled as a boolean rather than marginal relief.
findings.remediation: tax = min(slabTax, taxableIncome - threshold) above the threshold before cess.

findings.title: Old-regime surcharge capped at 25% above 5 crore (should be 37%)
findings.evidence: The same surcharge schedule, capped at 25%, is applied to both regimes.
findings.impact: High earners on the old regime are under-taxed.
findings.rootCause: Regime not branched in the surcharge calculation.
findings.remediation: Branch on regime; test at 50L, 1Cr, 2Cr, 5Cr and 5.01Cr.

findings.title: Mid-month joiners and leavers pay LOP for pre-joining and post-exit days
findings.evidence: Working days are counted for the whole month while paid days only include days with attendance logs.
findings.impact: A joiner on the 20th loses roughly two-thirds of the first salary; a leaver is penalised after their last day.
findings.remediation: Clip the working window to max(monthStart, joiningDate) and min(monthEnd, lastWorkingDay).

findings.title: Leave overlap, max-consecutive, eligibility, gender, attachment and half-day flags are not enforced
findings.evidence: The apply path validates balance and monthly ledger only. No reference to maxConsecutiveDays, applicableAfterDays, gender, attachmentRequired, halfDayAllowed or overlapping requests.
findings.impact: Policy configuration in the UI has no effect; employees can book overlapping or ineligible leave.
findings.rootCause: Rules stored as metadata but never implemented.
findings.remediation: Implement a validateLeaveRequest rule pipeline with one function per flag and per-rule tests.

findings.title: Any half-day request counts as 0.5 day regardless of date range
findings.evidence: isHalfDayCount returns 0.5 whenever isHalfDay is true.
findings.impact: A Monday-to-Friday half-day request consumes 0.5 instead of 2.5 days.
findings.remediation: Reject multi-day half-day requests or count 0.5 per date.

findings.title: Holiday queries fall back to every company's holidays when the tenant has none
findings.evidence: When the company-scoped holiday list is empty, the code re-queries holiday.findMany({}) with no company filter.
findings.impact: Other tenants' holidays are treated as non-working days, inflating paid days and reducing LOP.
findings.rootCause: Global fallback intended for parent-company sharing applied to all tenants.
findings.remediation: Remove the global fallback; treat only weekends as non-working when no calendar exists; warn on missing configuration.

findings.title: TDS is annual tax divided by 12 with no YTD true-up or declaration projection
findings.evidence: Monthly TDS is computed as annual liability divided by 12 with no year-to-date adjustment.
findings.impact: Under- or over-withholding across the year; year-end surprises and interest exposure.
findings.remediation: Maintain YTD taxable income and deductions, recompute monthly TDS with true-up.

findings.title: Professional tax is a fixed structure value with no state slabs
findings.evidence: Professional tax is read from the salary structure rather than computed from state rules.
findings.impact: Wrong deduction in most states.
findings.remediation: Load state-wise PT slabs per employee work location.

findings.title: Manual PF/ESI flags use inverted-looking semantics
findings.evidence: Manual amounts are selected when pfAsPerGovt === false (and likewise for ESI), which reads as inverted; payroll output was not executed to confirm.
findings.impact: Employees with manual statutory contributions may get the wrong amount.
findings.remediation: Rename to pfMode/esiMode with explicit values and migrate data; add payroll fixture tests.

findings.title: FnF gratuity and notice calculations are simplified and not configurable
findings.evidence: Gratuity and notice recovery use hardcoded formulas with no policy configuration; not validated against statute.
findings.impact: Settlement amounts may be legally wrong.
findings.remediation: Make formulas configurable and reviewed by legal; add golden FnF tests.

findings.title: Carry-forward limit and encashment flags are not applied at year rollover
findings.evidence: LeaveType stores carryForward, carryForwardLimit and encashment, but the rollover job does not read them.
findings.impact: Configured policy is ignored; balances roll over incorrectly.
findings.rootCause: Rollover job only copies or expires balances.
findings.remediation: Apply limits and encashment in the rollover transaction; add tests.

findings.title: Comp-off is auto-credited for working a weekly off without an approval workflow
findings.evidence: Comp-off is credited automatically when attendance is recorded on a weekly off.
findings.impact: Employees accrue extra leave without manager review; abuse and balance inflation.
findings.rootCause: Credit happens in the attendance path.
findings.remediation: Create a CompOffRequest requiring approval before crediting; make it policy-controlled.

findings.title: Late-penalty fallback constant (6) is used when no policy exists
findings.evidence: When no attendance policy is configured, a hardcoded maximum of 6 lates triggers a deduction.
findings.impact: Companies without a policy silently penalise employees.
findings.rootCause: Magic default instead of explicit configuration.
findings.remediation: Require an explicit policy or apply no penalty with a warning.

findings.title: Probation and confirmation have no workflow; probation is free text
findings.evidence: probation is a string field with no scheduled review or auto-confirmation.
findings.impact: Confirmation dates are never enforced; employees remain in probation indefinitely.
findings.remediation: Add probation end date, scheduled review tasks and auto-confirm/alert policies.

findings.title: Leave balances are deduplicated by type name, masking duplicate types
findings.evidence: Balance rows are merged on leaveType.name rather than id.
findings.impact: Two distinct leave types with the same name silently collapse; wrong balances shown.
findings.rootCause: Deduplication key uses a display string.
findings.remediation: Deduplicate by id and enforce a unique code per company.

findings.title: Payouts can be added after a cycle is locked, leaving payslips stale
findings.evidence: Additional payout creation does not check payroll cycle status or trigger recalculation.
findings.impact: Locked payslips no longer match recorded payouts.
findings.rootCause: Missing lock enforcement on payout mutation.
findings.remediation: Reject payouts on locked cycles or create a new adjustment cycle with recalculation.

findings.title: Updating a salary structure on an existing effective date writes a duplicate revision row
findings.evidence: setSalaryStructure creates a new row instead of updating when effectiveFrom matches.
findings.impact: Multiple revisions for one date; ambiguous 'latest' ordering feeds BL-003.
findings.remediation: Upsert on (employeeId, effectiveFrom); add the unique constraint from DB-006.

findings.title: Duplicate holidays on the same company and date are allowed and double-counted
findings.evidence: Holiday has no unique (companyId, date); day counting subtracts each holiday row.
findings.impact: One holiday can reduce working days twice.
findings.remediation: Add @@unique([companyId, date]) and deduplicate existing rows.

findings.title: Leave day counting excludes Sundays but ignores Saturday weekly-off rules
findings.evidence: Day counting iterates dates and skips Sundays only; resolveSaturdayWeeklyOff is not used.
findings.impact: Leave consumes the wrong number of days for 5-day and alternate-Saturday policies.
findings.rootCause: Attendance policy not consulted in leave counting.
findings.remediation: Reuse resolveSaturdayWeeklyOff and the company attendance policy.

findings.title: applicableAfterDays, gender, attachmentRequired and maxConsecutiveDays are dead configuration
findings.evidence: Fields exist on LeaveType but have no enforcement call sites.
findings.impact: Admins configure rules that do nothing.
findings.rootCause: Schema and UI ahead of implementation.
findings.remediation: Implement or remove from the UI until implemented.

findings.title: Payroll gross excludes employer PF/ESI while employee CTC is divided by 12
findings.evidence: CTC is treated as a monthly total while payroll gross omits employer contributions.
findings.impact: Offer letters show a CTC that payroll never pays; reconciliation disputes.
findings.rootCause: CTC and gross component models are conflated.
findings.remediation: Define CTC components explicitly and show employer contributions separately.

findings.title: Employee delete is a hard delete cascading across 58 relations
findings.evidence: remove() calls employee.delete; Employee has 58 onDelete: Cascade relations including Payslip, AttendanceLog, LeaveRequest, TaxDeclaration and EmployeeDocument.
findings.impact: Irreversible loss of payroll and attendance history that may be legally required.
findings.rootCause: Hard delete with cascades on statutory records.
findings.remediation: Soft delete (status terminated, deletedAt); restrict hard delete to a maintenance path; use onDelete: Restrict for payroll/attendance.

findings.title: AttendanceLog has no unique (employeeId, date)
findings.evidence: Only @@index([employeeId, date]) exists; duplicate day rows are possible.
findings.impact: Duplicate attendance rows double-count paid days and corrupt payroll (see BL-002).
findings.remediation: Add @@unique([employeeId, date]) after deduplicating existing rows.

findings.title: Payslip has no unique (employeeId, payrollCycleId)
findings.evidence: No unique constraint; the run loop uses findFirst then create/update.
findings.impact: Concurrent or retried payroll runs can create duplicate payslips.
findings.remediation: Add the unique constraint and use upsert; add idempotency (API-011).

findings.title: PermissionRequest has no unique key for (employeeId, date, fromTime)
findings.evidence: No unique constraint on the natural key.
findings.impact: Duplicate corrective requests; conflicting approvals.
findings.remediation: Add the unique constraint and handle conflicts explicitly.

findings.title: Holiday has no unique (companyId, date)
findings.evidence: No unique constraint on company and date.
findings.impact: Duplicate holidays double-count working days (BL-022).
findings.remediation: Add @@unique([companyId, date]) and deduplicate.

findings.title: SalaryStructure has no unique (employeeId, effectiveFrom) and no companyId
findings.evidence: No unique constraint and no direct companyId column; tenant scoping relies on the employee relation.
findings.impact: Duplicate revisions and awkward tenant queries; feeds BL-003/BL-021.
findings.rootCause: Missing constraint and denormalized tenant key.
findings.remediation: Add unique (employeeId, effectiveFrom); consider companyId for index/scope.

findings.title: Money and leave balances use Float instead of Decimal
findings.evidence: Payroll and balance columns are typed Float.
findings.impact: Floating-point drift in payroll totals and leave balances.
findings.remediation: Migrate to Decimal(12,2) / Decimal(6,2) and add rounding tests.

findings.title: User.email is globally unique, preventing the same email in two tenants
findings.evidence: @unique on email at the table level.
findings.impact: The same person cannot hold accounts in two tenants; login is ambiguous in a multi-tenant model.
findings.remediation: Use @@unique([companyId, email]) plus an explicit cross-tenant identity table.

findings.title: Role has no unique (companyId, name)
findings.evidence: No uniqueness on role name within a company.
findings.impact: Duplicate roles with divergent grants; name-based authorization becomes ambiguous.
findings.remediation: Add @@unique([companyId, name]) and deduplicate.

findings.title: No soft-delete or retention columns on core HR entities
findings.evidence: No deletedAt/archivedAt fields on Employee, Payslip, AttendanceLog and related models.
findings.impact: Accidental or malicious deletion is unrecoverable; no retention policy support.
findings.remediation: Add deletedAt plus query scoping; define retention windows.

findings.title: Status fields are free-form strings with no check constraints
findings.evidence: Status and type columns are String with defaults; no enums or checks.
findings.impact: Typo or case variance creates unreachable states and broken filters.
findings.remediation: Use Prisma enums or check constraints; migrate existing values.

findings.title: Prisma schema is valid but fails prisma format --check
findings.evidence: npx prisma validate passes; npx prisma format --check reports formatting differences.
findings.impact: Noisy diffs and review friction; formatting drift hides real changes.
findings.remediation: Run prisma format and add a CI check.

findings.title: docker-compose provisions PostgreSQL while Prisma uses MySQL
findings.evidence: Compose starts postgres:16-alpine and redis; README refers to a non-existent hrms-mysql service; Prisma provider is mysql.
findings.impact: New developer setup fails or runs the wrong engine.
findings.remediation: Replace Compose services with MySQL (and required dependencies) or update the schema/README consistently.

findings.title: Render deploy never runs prisma migrate deploy
findings.evidence: buildCommand runs prisma generate and nest build; startCommand runs node dist/main. No migrate step anywhere.
findings.impact: A fresh or restored deployment starts against an unmigrated schema and fails at runtime.
findings.rootCause: Missing migration step in deployment config.
findings.remediation: Add npx prisma migrate deploy as a pre-deploy command and fail the deploy on error.

findings.title: Json columns (breakdown, companySnapshot, metadata) are unvalidated
findings.evidence: Json fields accept arbitrary structure with no runtime validation.
findings.impact: Malformed JSON breaks payslip rendering and audit reconstruction.
findings.remediation: Validate with Zod on write and version the payload shape.

findings.title: Cascading deletes bypass application-level retention and business rules
findings.evidence: 58 cascading deletes, 3 SetNull, 2 Restrict across the schema.
findings.impact: Parent deletions silently erase regulated records without application checks.
findings.remediation: Use Restrict for payroll/attendance/document relations and handle deletion explicitly in services.

findings.title: Live migration history vs schema drift could not be verified
findings.evidence: No authorised database connection was available; prisma migrate status was not run against any environment.
findings.impact: Unknown risk that production schema differs from migrations.
findings.remediation: Run prisma migrate status against a restored copy and add a drift check to deployment.

findings.title: Platform guard accepts macOS despite Windows-only product copy
findings.evidence: evaluatePlatform returns supported: true for darwin while the dialog copy states Windows 10/11 only.
findings.impact: Unsupported platforms are admitted and then fail unpredictably.
findings.rootCause: Guard logic and product copy diverge.
findings.remediation: Define one supported-platform constant and reject anything outside it; align copy.

findings.title: Unparseable Windows version fails open (supported: true)
findings.evidence: When osVersion cannot be parsed, the guard returns supported: true.
findings.impact: A malformed or spoofed version string bypasses the Windows 10/11 check.
findings.remediation: Fail closed on parse failure; surface a clear error.

findings.title: Windows and macOS builds are unsigned
findings.evidence: mac.identity null, mac.sign false, no Windows certificate, CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false.
findings.impact: SmartScreen/Gatekeeper warnings; users cannot verify publisher integrity.
findings.remediation: Sign Windows with Authenticode, sign and notarize macOS, set publisherName.

findings.title: Updater verifies SHA-512 but not publisher or signature
findings.evidence: electron-updater checks the sha512 in latest.yml; no publisherName or signature verification is configured.
findings.impact: A compromised GitHub release can deliver an unsigned update that passes the checksum check.
findings.remediation: Add code signing and publisher verification; sign the manifest assets.

findings.title: No win.publisherName configured
findings.evidence: The win block contains target and icon only.
findings.impact: Updater cannot verify the Authenticode publisher.
findings.remediation: Set win.publisherName once signing is enabled.

findings.title: Release publishes if either platform succeeds; manual runs fall back to v3.1.1
findings.evidence: Publish condition is OR of build-windows and build-macos results; tag_name falls back to the literal v3.1.1 when not on a tag ref.
findings.impact: Partial releases and manual runs that overwrite or attach mismatched assets to an existing version.
findings.remediation: Require both jobs, derive tag from package.json, fail on mismatch, add a concurrency lock.

findings.title: Renderer overwrites the main-process device id with a localStorage UUID
findings.evidence: When desktop context exists the renderer spreads it and replaces deviceId with getDeviceId() from localStorage.
findings.impact: Device identity in security logs is client-controlled and resettable.
findings.rootCause: Renderer substitution of a trusted main-process value.
findings.remediation: Preserve desktop.deviceId; send any renderer value as a separate untrusted signal.

findings.title: IPC sender guard accepts any file:// URL
findings.evidence: if (url.startsWith('file://')) return true;
findings.impact: Any local HTML page receives the full privileged preload API.
findings.rootCause: Prefix check instead of exact URL comparison.
findings.remediation: Compare against pathToFileURL(rendererIndex).href exactly.

findings.title: No load-failure or renderer-crash handling; splash can hang
findings.evidence: Splash closes only on ready-to-show; no did-fail-load, render-process-gone or unresponsive handlers.
findings.impact: A renderer failure leaves a permanent splash or blank window with no recovery.
findings.remediation: Add failure/crash handlers that close the splash, show an error page and offer retry/quit.

findings.title: macOS in-app update cannot work (latest-mac.yml absent, unsigned)
findings.evidence: dmg.writeUpdateInfo is false so latest-mac.yml is not generated; the published release has none; installUpdate opens GitHub on darwin.
findings.impact: Mac users never receive an in-app update.
findings.rootCause: Update metadata and signing not configured for macOS.
findings.remediation: Sign and notarize, generate latest-mac.yml, or remove the auto-update claim and document manual download.

findings.title: CSP may not apply to file:// and there is no meta fallback
findings.evidence: CSP is injected only via ses.webRequest.onHeadersReceived; Electron does not guarantee interception of file:// loads; index.html has no meta CSP. Runtime interception was not tested.
findings.impact: Either the packaged app runs with no CSP, or inline theme script and Google Fonts are blocked.
findings.remediation: Add a meta CSP or serve the renderer over a custom protocol; align script-src/font-src.

findings.title: Packaged renderer may send Origin: null which backend CORS rejects
findings.evidence: Backend allows a missing Origin (if (!origin)) but not the literal string 'null'. A file:// document sends Origin: null on cross-origin fetch. Not tested against the packaged app.
findings.impact: If confirmed, login, refresh and every authenticated screen fail in the packaged desktop app.
findings.rootCause: file:// opaque origin not considered in CORS policy.
findings.remediation: Run a packaged smoke test capturing Origin; allow null narrowly for the desktop client or move to a custom app:// protocol.

findings.title: In-process cron on Render free plan sleeps with the service
findings.evidence: plan: free; @Cron jobs run inside the web process, which Render suspends after inactivity.
findings.impact: Attendance auto-marking, leave accrual and scheduled announcements can be skipped entirely.
findings.rootCause: Scheduled work co-located with an ephemeral web process.
findings.remediation: Use an always-on instance or an external scheduler/worker.

findings.title: Blocking OS probes run before the splash is shown
findings.evidence: collectDeviceContext() runs synchronous reg, tasklist, wmic/PowerShell probes with 5-6 second timeouts before createSplashWindow().
findings.impact: Appears hung for tens of seconds on slow or locked-down machines.
findings.rootCause: Synchronous startup probing on the main thread.
findings.remediation: Show the splash first, run probes asynchronously with caching and an overall startup budget.

findings.title: No desktop CI job; tracked out/*.js is stale
findings.evidence: CI has only backend and frontend jobs. Tracked out/main/main.js lacks the https://*.onrender.com CSP entry present in source.
findings.impact: TypeScript errors and stale compiled code can ship unnoticed.
findings.rootCause: Desktop project excluded from CI and build output committed.
findings.remediation: Add a desktop CI job (tsc --noEmit, electron-vite build); stop tracking desktop/out/.

findings.title: copy:renderer merges into an existing directory, shipping stale bundles
findings.evidence: fs.cpSync without prior removal; local renderer contains 678 files across five build dates vs 158 in a clean build.
findings.impact: Local installers ship stale code; builds are not reproducible.
findings.remediation: Delete dist/renderer before copying; build releases only in CI.

findings.title: Electron 33 is end-of-life
findings.evidence: Electron 33.4.11 pinned; Electron supports the latest three majors only.
findings.impact: Chromium security fixes are no longer backported to a payroll/PII application.
findings.remediation: Upgrade to a supported major and add a quarterly check.

findings.title: Report Issue links to the wrong GitHub organization
findings.evidence: Menu opens https://github.com/Workora/hrms/issues while the repository is lordsandkings85-ship-it/hrms.
findings.impact: Users cannot report issues.
findings.remediation: Point at the real repository or remove the item.

findings.title: Payroll runs serial per-employee queries inside one interactive transaction
findings.evidence: Inside $transaction the loop issues payslip.findFirst then update/create per employee.
findings.impact: For 500 employees this is over 1,000 round-trips holding locks; risk of timeout and blocked payroll.
findings.remediation: Precompute rows, use createMany/upsert batches, move email work outside the transaction; benchmark 500 employees.

findings.title: ExcelJS 938 kB and jsPDF 357 kB are in the main bundle
findings.evidence: Production build reports exceljs 938.27 kB, charts 421 kB, jspdf 357 kB, PayslipPreviewModal 340 kB, index 227 kB.
findings.impact: Slow first load on web and slower renderer startup on desktop.
findings.rootCause: Static imports of heavy export libraries.
findings.remediation: Dynamic-import Excel/PDF only on export; lazy-load chart routes.

findings.title: refetchOnMount always plus focus refetch reloads lists repeatedly
findings.evidence: QueryClient defaults force refetch on mount and on window focus with no staleTime.
findings.impact: Elevated API load and UI flicker; amplifies PERF-006 and PERF-001 contention.
findings.remediation: Set staleTime and targeted invalidation; disable refetchOnMount always.

findings.title: Unbounded list endpoints load entire tenants into memory
findings.evidence: findMany without take/skip on tenant-wide collections.
findings.impact: Memory and latency grow linearly with tenant size.
findings.remediation: Enforce caps and cursor pagination.

findings.title: No composite index for attendance date-range queries per tenant
findings.evidence: AttendanceLog has @@index([employeeId, date]) but no company-scoped or date-first index for payroll-wide scans.
findings.impact: Payroll and attendance reports do full or wide scans at scale.
findings.rootCause: Indexes designed for single-employee lookup only.
findings.remediation: Add indexes matching actual query predicates; verify with EXPLAIN on a restored copy.

findings.title: isGroupWideUser performs a user+role+permission query on nearly every request
findings.evidence: Each call loads the user with role permissions; it is invoked from guards and multiple services per request.
findings.impact: Extra DB round-trips on hot paths.
findings.rootCause: Authorization data not cached on the session/token.
findings.remediation: Resolve capabilities once at login and cache on the session with short TTL/invalidation.

findings.title: Permission cache is per-process with 5-minute TTL and no invalidation
findings.evidence: In-memory Map with CACHE_TTL_MS 5 minutes; no pub/sub or per-instance coordination.
findings.impact: Revoked permissions persist up to 5 minutes; instances disagree.
findings.remediation: Shorten TTL, invalidate on role change, or use a shared cache with events.

findings.title: Recharts chunk is 421 kB and loaded for dashboard charts
findings.evidence: Chart vendor chunk is 421 kB in the production build.
findings.impact: Large payload for users who only view the dashboard.
findings.remediation: Lazy-load chart routes or use a lighter chart library.

findings.title: Monolithic page components prevent effective route-level code splitting
findings.evidence: OrganizationPage and AdvancedEmployeeForm are imported statically at route level and exceed 1,400 lines.
findings.impact: Large initial chunks and unnecessary re-renders.
findings.remediation: Split components and use React.lazy per route.

findings.title: Verbose console.log output in backend hot paths
findings.evidence: console.log statements remain in request and payroll paths.
findings.impact: Log noise, cost and potential data leakage in logs.
findings.remediation: Use a leveled structured logger and redact PII.

findings.title: Prisma queries return full rows including encrypted PII where select would do
findings.evidence: Several findMany calls omit select, pulling encrypted PII columns that are then decrypted.
findings.impact: Over-fetch and unnecessary decrypt cost; wider data exposure in memory.
findings.remediation: Use explicit select per endpoint and decrypt only needed fields.

findings.title: No Prisma connection-pool sizing for a serverless/free-tier host
findings.evidence: No connection_limit in DATABASE_URL and no pool configuration; free-tier connection caps are low. Runtime behaviour not measured.
findings.impact: Connection exhaustion under concurrency.
findings.remediation: Set an explicit connection limit appropriate to the host and monitor.

findings.title: No self-service password reset / forgot-password flow
findings.evidence: Only admin reset exists; no request-reset or reset-with-token endpoint and no UI.
findings.impact: Users locked out depend on an admin; blocks self-service operation.
findings.remediation: Add single-use, short-lived reset tokens with rate limiting and email delivery.

findings.title: No E2E or packaged-app smoke tests
findings.evidence: Only backend unit tests exist; there is no Playwright/Cypress and no packaged smoke script.
findings.impact: Release-blocking defects such as DESK-012 and FE-001 cannot be caught before release.
findings.remediation: Add Playwright for web and a packaged smoke script covering login, list fetch and updater manifest.

findings.title: MFA lifecycle incomplete (verify/disable/recovery)
findings.evidence: Enable-only implementation; no verification, disable or recovery codes.
findings.impact: MFA cannot be safely operated.
findings.remediation: Complete the TOTP lifecycle and audit events.

findings.title: No audit-log viewer for security and PII access
findings.evidence: AuditLog is persisted but no admin UI or query API exposes it.
findings.impact: Security events cannot be investigated by administrators.
findings.remediation: Add a filtered audit viewer with export and retention.

findings.title: Statutory returns (PF ECR, ESIC, 24Q, PT) are not generated
findings.evidence: Compliance masters exist but no export generators were found; not exercised at runtime.
findings.impact: Compliance filing must be done outside the system.
findings.remediation: Implement statutory export formats with validation and reconciliation.

findings.title: No bank/NEFT payout file export
findings.evidence: Payroll computes net pay only; no bank file generator.
findings.impact: Bulk salary payment must be prepared manually.
findings.remediation: Add NEFT/CSV export with account validation and checksum.

findings.title: Email delivery has no queue, retry or observability
findings.evidence: Direct send call with no Bull queue despite @nestjs/bull being a dependency.
findings.impact: Lost payslip and notification emails; failures invisible.
findings.remediation: Queue sends, add retries, DLQ and delivery metrics.

findings.title: No documented backup, restore or disaster-recovery procedure
findings.evidence: No runbook; the only SQL backups found are the committed dumps.
findings.impact: Unproven recovery; risk of extended outage or data loss.
findings.remediation: Document and rehearse restore; automate encrypted off-site backups.

findings.title: No account lockout or CAPTCHA after repeated failures
findings.evidence: Only IP-based throttling; no account counter.
findings.impact: Distributed credential stuffing remains viable.
findings.remediation: Add per-account lockout, CAPTCHA and alerting.

findings.title: No document virus or malware scanning
findings.evidence: No scanning integration and URLs are client-supplied.
findings.impact: Malicious files can be distributed to HR users.
findings.remediation: Scan uploads with ClamAV or a cloud scanner before making them available.

findings.title: No internationalisation or localisation
findings.evidence: All strings are hardcoded English; no i18n framework.
findings.impact: Cannot serve non-English locales.
findings.remediation: Extract strings and add a locale layer with date/number formatting.

findings.title: No accessibility conformance target or audit
findings.evidence: No axe/WCAG checks in CI and no documented target; static review suggests gaps (FE-016).
findings.impact: Legal and usability risk for employees with disabilities.
findings.rootCause: Accessibility not in the definition of done.
findings.remediation: Adopt WCAG 2.2 AA and run automated plus manual audits.
